# Nucleus

> Nucleus is a Kotlin framework for building native cross-platform desktop apps on top of Compose Multiplatform. It combines a Gradle plugin, runtime libraries, and GitHub Actions to handle OS integration (30+ runtime modules), packaging (18 distribution formats), performance (GraalVM Native Image and JVM AOT cache), and native window decorations (Tao backend).

- Docs: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs
- GitHub: https://github.com/NucleusFramework/Nucleus
- Gradle Plugin Portal: https://plugins.gradle.org/plugin/dev.nucleusframework
- Maven Central: https://central.sonatype.com/search?q=dev.nucleusframework
- License: Apache 2.0 / MIT

## Documentation
- [Welcome to Nucleus 3.0](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs): Nucleus adds native windows, OS integration, and packaging to Compose Multiplatform desktop apps written in Kotlin.

### Get started

  - [Install](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/start/install): Apply the Nucleus Gradle plugin to a Kotlin project to build for macOS, Linux, and Windows from one build.
  - [Quickstart](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/start/quickstart): Build and run your first Nucleus desktop app, then package it as a native installer.
  - [Configuration](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/start/configuration): Write the minimal nucleus.application { } block a new app needs, then find the page that covers each packaging, runtime, and OS integration option.

### Migrate

  - [Migrate from Nucleus 2.x to 3.0](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/migrate/from-2.x): Move a Nucleus 2.x app to 3.0. Remove the backend choice and the AWT windows, switch the window state import, and review the runtime and build changes.
  - [Migrate from JetBrains Compose Desktop](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/migrate/from-jb-compose): Move a JetBrains Compose Desktop app to Nucleus. Apply the plugin, rename the DSL block, and replace the AWT windows, dialogs, and tray with their Nucleus equivalents.
  - [Migrate with an AI agent](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/migrate/ai-agent): Point an AI coding agent at the Nucleus migration playbook or at the 3.0 upgrade guide, and let it migrate your app one verified step at a time.

### Concepts

  - [Architecture](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/concepts/architecture): The layers of a Nucleus application, where AWT still runs, and how native libraries ship.
  - [Modules](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/concepts/modules): The Nucleus Gradle modules, what nucleus-application brings with it, and how to add the rest.
  - [Threading](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/concepts/threading): The UI thread that runs Compose under Nucleus, which callbacks reach it, how to port Swing-style code, and the Windows event-loop watchdog.

### Windows

  - [Windows](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/windows): Open native desktop windows from Compose with nucleusApplication and DecoratedWindow, set their chrome, and route secondary windows through a host.
  - [Window state](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/windows/window-state): Control and observe window size, position, placement, and screen with Compose's WindowState or the AWT-free window API v2 in dev.nucleusframework.window.tao.v2.
  - [Window scaffold and chrome](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/windows/window-scaffold): Build full-window layouts and custom title bars with WindowScaffold, drag areas, WindowControls, and the macOS and Windows 11 materials.
  - [Dialogs and popups](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/windows/dialogs-popups): Open modal dialogs with DecoratedDialog, HostedDialog, or a toolkit dialog, and render Compose popups as native surfaces placed against the screen.
  - [Overlay windows](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/windows/overlay-windows): Build watermarks, desktop widgets, and heads-up overlays with transparent, click-through, always-on-bottom, and all-workspaces windows.
  - [Linux and Wayland](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/windows/linux-wayland): How Nucleus windows run on native Wayland and X11, what the compositor controls, and how to branch on screen placement.
  - [HiDPI and text rendering](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/windows/hidpi): How Nucleus windows follow each monitor's scale factor, and how ClearType text works on Windows.

### Toolkits

  - [Toolkits](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/toolkits): macOS 26, Fluent, Yaru, Jewel, and Material restyle the Nucleus window for each desktop design language.
  - [macOS 26](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/toolkits/macos): A Compose Multiplatform macOS 26 design system with Liquid Glass materials and a Nucleus decorated window.
  - [Fluent](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/toolkits/fluent): Windows 11 Fluent UI for Compose Multiplatform, with a Nucleus FluentDecoratedWindow.
  - [Yaru](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/toolkits/yaru): Ubuntu Yaru widgets and themes for Compose Multiplatform, with a Nucleus YaruDecoratedWindow.
  - [Jewel](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/toolkits/jewel): Style a Nucleus window with Jewel colors and metrics so the title bar and chrome match the IntelliJ Platform.
  - [Material 2 and 3](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/toolkits/material): Theme a Nucleus window from a Compose MaterialTheme with the Material 2 or Material 3 adapter.

### Tool windows

  - [Tool windows](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/tool-windows): Satellite palettes that dock and Chrome-like tabs that tear off, and the workspace model they share.
  - [Satellites](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/tool-windows/satellites): Declare tool palettes and inspectors once, let them follow the focused document window, dock them, and save the layout.
  - [Docking](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/tool-windows/docking): Lay docked satellites out around your content with DockLayout, size and order the panels, restrict where they go, and draw your own splitters.
  - [Tabs](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/tool-windows/tabs): Declare documents as Chrome-like tabs that reorder, tear off into windows and merge back, with custom strips, previews and saved layouts.

### Input

  - [Trackpad gestures](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/input/trackpad-gestures): Handle trackpad scrolling, pinch-to-zoom and rotation with standard Compose modifiers.
  - [Mouse buttons](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/input/mouse-buttons): Handle the back and forward side buttons of a mouse as Compose pointer buttons.
  - [Pen and touch input](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/input/pen-stylus): Read touchscreen and pen contacts, with pressure, from Compose pointer events.
  - [Drag and drop](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/input/drag-and-drop): Receive files dropped on a window and drag files or text out of it with the Compose drag-and-drop API.
  - [Pointer icons](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/input/pointer-icons): Show grab, move, wait, help and resize cursors with TaoPointerIcons and Modifier.pointerHoverIcon.
  - [Accessibility](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/input/accessibility): Expose your Compose semantics to VoiceOver, Narrator, Orca and UI automation tools.

### Native content

  - [Native views](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/native-content/native-views): Embed an NSView, HWND or GtkWidget inside a Compose layout with NativeView.
  - [TextureView](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/native-content/texture-view): Draw a GPU texture from an external producer inside the Compose scene, with no CPU frame copy.
  - [GPU render context](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/native-content/gpu-render-context): Give an in-process renderer the scene's Skia DirectContext and GPU device, so it draws without a second device or a per-frame copy.

### PDF reader

  - [PDF reader](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/pdf): Render PDFs, extract text, and select or copy content from Compose, with one API across Android, iOS, web, and desktop.
  - [Getting started](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/pdf/getting-started): Load PDF bytes, react to loading state, and enable text selection, links, thumbnails, and zoom.
  - [API reference](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/pdf/api-reference): PdfReaderState, PdfPage, PdfThumbnail, PdfReader, and the supporting data types.

### WebView

  - [WebView](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/webview): Embed a native web engine in Compose with one API across Android, iOS, web, and desktop.
  - [Getting started](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/webview/getting-started): Load URLs and HTML, navigate the history stack, evaluate JavaScript, and intercept requests from Compose.
  - [API reference](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/webview/api-reference): WebView, WebViewState, WebViewNavigator, settings, cookies, JS bridge, and request interception.

### OS integration

  - [OS integration](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os): Kotlin modules for native desktop features on macOS, Windows, and Linux, such as notifications, the system tray, global hotkeys, media controls, dark mode, and accent color.

#### Notifications

    - [Cross-platform notifications](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/notifications): Send desktop notifications on macOS, Windows, and Linux from a single Kotlin API.
    - [Notifications on macOS](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/notifications/macos): Kotlin bindings for Apple's UserNotifications framework, with authorization, categories, attachments, text input, triggers, and interruption levels.
    - [Notifications on Windows](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/notifications/windows): Send Windows toast notifications from Kotlin with adaptive text, images, buttons, inputs, headers, and progress bars.
    - [Notifications on Linux](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/notifications/linux): Send freedesktop desktop notifications over D-Bus from Kotlin, with urgency, hints, sounds, images, and action callbacks.

#### System tray

    - [System tray](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/tray): Draw a tray icon and its native menu from Compose on macOS, Windows, and Linux without AWT.
    - [Tray menu DSL](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/tray/menu): Build the tray context menu in Kotlin with items, checkable items, submenus, dividers, shortcut hints, and state-driven content.
    - [Tray-anchored apps](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/tray/tray-app): TrayApp opens a Compose popup window next to a system tray icon, for menu bar and tray utilities written in Kotlin.

#### Dock and taskbar

    - [Dock and taskbar](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/dock-taskbar): Progress, badges and menus on the macOS Dock, the Windows taskbar and the Linux launcher.
    - [macOS Dock menu](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/dock-taskbar/macos): Populate the Dock right-click menu of a macOS app with items, submenus, and separators, and handle clicks from Kotlin.
    - [Windows taskbar](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/dock-taskbar/windows): Drive the Windows taskbar from Kotlin with overlay icons, jump lists, thumbnail toolbar buttons, and badges.
    - [Linux launcher](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/dock-taskbar/linux): Set count badges, progress bars, urgency flags, and right-click quicklist menus on the Linux launcher from Kotlin.
    - [Progress and attention](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/dock-taskbar/progress): Show progress and attention requests on the Dock icon, the taskbar button, or the Linux launcher entry from Kotlin.

#### Menus

    - [macOS menu bar](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/menus/menu-bar): Build the native macOS menu bar from Compose, with items, shortcuts, icons, badges, and submenus that follow your state.
    - [Context menus](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/menus/context-menu): Replace Compose-drawn context menus with the platform menu, NSMenu on macOS and a Fluent, Adwaita, or Breeze flyout on Windows and Linux.
  - [File dialogs](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/file-dialogs): Open, save and folder pickers with FileKit, set up for you by nucleusApplication.
  - [Global hotkeys](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/global-hotkey): Register system-wide keyboard shortcuts that fire while your app is in the background.
  - [Media controls](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/media-control): Publish now-playing metadata to the system media center and receive playback commands on macOS, Windows, and Linux from Kotlin.
  - [Spell check](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/spell-check): Check spelling in Compose text fields with each operating system's engine, NSSpellChecker on macOS, the Windows Spell Checking API, and Hunspell on Linux.

#### Theme

    - [Dark mode detector](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/theme/dark-mode): Read the operating system's light or dark theme from Kotlin and recompose your Compose UI when it changes.
    - [System accent color](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/theme/accent-color): Read the user's OS accent color and high-contrast setting as Compose state that follows system changes.

#### Icons

    - [SF Symbols](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/icons/sf-symbols): Typed Kotlin constants for Apple SF Symbols names used by macOS APIs.
    - [FreeDesktop icon names](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/icons/freedesktop): Typed Kotlin constants for the names defined by the FreeDesktop Icon Naming Specification.
  - [System info](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/system-info): Read host details such as the OS, CPU, memory, disks, GPUs, batteries, network, processes, and users through the SystemInfo object.

### Lifecycle

  - [Lifecycle](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/lifecycle): The modules that connect a Nucleus app to OS events and services that outlive a single window.
  - [Application entry point](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/lifecycle/application): Start a Nucleus app with nucleusApplication, and control how it quits, locks to one instance, and initializes FileKit.
  - [Single instance](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/lifecycle/single-instance): Keep one running instance of your app and forward a second launch's deep link to the primary process.
  - [Deep links and URL schemes](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/lifecycle/deep-links): Register a custom URL scheme at packaging time and receive the incoming deep-link URI in your Nucleus app.

#### Background work

    - [Launch at login](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/lifecycle/background/launch-at-login): Enable, disable, and query launch at login from Kotlin with one API that picks the backend for the current packaging format.
    - [Scheduler](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/lifecycle/background/scheduler): Run periodic, calendar, and on-boot background tasks from Kotlin that the OS fires on schedule, even when your app is closed.
    - [Scheduler testing](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/lifecycle/background/scheduler-testing): Test doubles for the scheduler that run background tasks in memory, with virtual time and controllable constraints.
    - [Service management (macOS)](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/lifecycle/background/service-management): Register login items, launch agents, and launch daemons through the macOS SMAppService API from Kotlin.
  - [Energy manager](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/lifecycle/energy-manager): Lower your app's OS scheduling priority in the background and keep the system or display awake from Kotlin.
  - [Filesystem watcher](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/lifecycle/fs-watcher): Watch files and directories from Kotlin and collect create, modify, remove, and move events as a coroutine Flow.
  - [App metadata at runtime](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/lifecycle/app-metadata): Read your app's id, version, vendor, display name, and Windows AUMID from Kotlin at runtime.
  - [Executable type](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/lifecycle/executable-type): Detect at runtime how the app was packaged and whether it runs in an OS sandbox, from a DMG or Snap to a plain ./gradlew run.

### Packaging & distribution

  - [Packaging overview](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/packaging): Declare the installer formats your app ships in the Nucleus Gradle DSL and build each one the host operating system supports.
  - [Building for macOS](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/packaging/macos): Package a Nucleus app for macOS as a DMG, a Developer ID PKG, or a Mac App Store PKG, embed app extensions, and build a universal binary.
  - [Building for Windows](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/packaging/windows): Package a Nucleus app for Windows as an NSIS, MSI, AppX, or Portable build, and see how the Windows renderer's ANGLE libraries ship.
  - [Building for Linux](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/packaging/linux): Build DEB, RPM, AppImage, and Pacman packages for a Nucleus app, add maintainer scripts, and package for the Snap Store and Flathub.
  - [Code signing](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/packaging/code-signing): Sign and notarize macOS builds, sign Windows installers with a PFX certificate or Azure Artifact Signing, and GPG-sign DEB and RPM packages.
  - [Sandboxing](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/packaging/sandboxing): Build the Mac App Store PKG, AppX, and Flatpak through the sandboxed pipeline, and detect the sandbox at runtime.
  - [Trusted CA certificates](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/packaging/trusted-certificates): Import private root CA certificates into the Java runtime bundled with your packaged app so its HTTPS calls trust them.
  - [Auto-update](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/packaging/auto-update): Check for, download, verify, and install application updates from Kotlin with updater-runtime, without a third-party service.
  - [Test updates](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/packaging/test-updates): Try the update UI, a real download and a full install against your next build, without publishing a release.
  - [Publishing](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/packaging/publishing): Configure where Nucleus publishes installers and auto-update metadata (GitHub Releases, S3, or a generic HTTPS host) and submit store builds.
  - [CI/CD](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/packaging/ci-cd): Build, sign, and publish a Nucleus desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux on GitHub Actions with the composite actions in the Nucleus repository.

### Performance & native

  - [Runtimes and performance](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/performance): Build the same Kotlin source as a GraalVM native image or as a JDK image with an AOT cache, pick the right one, and detect the runtime from code.
  - [Startup optimization](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/performance/startup): Turn on the nucleusOptimization pack to shorten JVM startup and lower idle memory, and package the app with the current OpenJDK through lastJdk.
  - [AOT cache](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/performance/aot-cache): Generate a Project Leyden AOT cache at build time and ship it in every installer, so the JVM skips most of its warmup at launch.

#### GraalVM Native Image

    - [GraalVM Native Image](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/performance/graalvm): Compile a Nucleus app ahead of time into a self-contained native binary. The plugin provisions GraalVM and generates the reachability metadata for you.
    - [Configuration](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/performance/graalvm/configuration): Reference for the graalvm { } block that configures native-image builds, including the toolchain, garbage collector, build arguments, PGO, the metadata repository, and per-OS settings.
    - [Automatic metadata](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/performance/graalvm/automatic-metadata): The Nucleus plugin generates GraalVM reachability metadata at build time. Fill the gaps with the tracing agent and prune your own entries.
    - [Tasks and CI](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/performance/graalvm/tasks-ci): The Gradle tasks the Nucleus plugin adds for GraalVM Native Image, where their output lands, and how to build on each OS in GitHub Actions.
  - [Native library loader](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/performance/native-library-loader): How Nucleus modules load their JNI libraries, from the folder next to a packaged app, the library path, or a content-addressed cache you can relocate.
  - [Native code in Kotlin](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/performance/native-code): Write platform code in Kotlin/Native and call it from the JVM as a Kotlin API. The NucleusNativeAccess plugin generates the FFM bridge, the JVM proxies and the GraalVM metadata.
  - [Native HTTP](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/performance/native-http): Configure java.net.http.HttpClient, OkHttp or Ktor to trust the operating system certificate store through NativeTrustManager.
  - [Native SSL](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/performance/native-ssl): Read the trusted certificates of the operating system and merge them with the JVM defaults into one X509TrustManager.
  - [Benchmarks](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/performance/benchmarks): Measured results of one CPU, rendering and list-load suite run inside a Compose desktop app on the JVM, GraalVM Native Image, SwiftUI, Tauri and Flutter.

### Reference

  - [Gradle DSL reference](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/reference/gradle-dsl): Every property and sub-block of the nucleus { } Gradle extension, checked against the plugin source.
  - [Troubleshooting](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/reference/troubleshooting): Common build, packaging, signing, and runtime problems in Nucleus, with the cause and fix for each.

### Compare

  - [Compare](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/compare): How Nucleus compares with vanilla Compose Multiplatform, with other JVM packaging tools, and with Electron and Tauri.
  - [Nucleus and vanilla Compose Multiplatform](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/compare/cmp-default): What Nucleus adds to JetBrains Compose Desktop and what it changes, as a decision guide for Kotlin teams shipping desktop apps.
  - [Packaging compared](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/compare/packaging): How Nucleus packaging compares with jpackage, Compose Multiplatform, Conveyor, install4j, jDeploy and JavaPackager on formats, auto-update, signing, CI, and stores.
- [Roadmap](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/roadmap): Planned Nucleus modules, APIs still experimental, work that waits on upstream projects, and features under consideration.
- [Changelog](https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/changelog): Release notes for every Nucleus release, newest first.
